parts: Name this game theory scenario in which two participants can either betray their partner to reduce their sentence, or both stay silent to share a commuted sentence.
This remarkably simple strategy won multiple repeated prisoner’s dilemma tournaments hosted by Robert Axelrod. In this strategy, one mimics an opponent’s previous move.

With Robert Keohane (“CO-han”), Axelrod applied his work on the prisoner’s dilemma to study how these things foster international cooperation. The “inclusive” type of these things lead to growth according to Why Nations Fail.
